function.name: calculate_Bond_Price
function.description: Calculate the bond price based on its face value, coupon rate, required rate of return, and the number of years until maturity. The calculation assumes annual coupon payments. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

Face_Value.description: The nominal value or par value of the bond in dollars. This is a float type value.

Coupon_rate.description: The annual coupon rate of the bond expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

Required_return.description: The annual required rate of return for the bond investment expressed as a percentage (e.g., 5 for 5%). This is a float type value.

maturity_years.description: The number of whole years until the bond's maturity.

message.content:
I’m sorry—I don’t have access to live market feeds, so I can’t tell you the exact spot‑price of gold right now.  

If you need an accurate, up‑to‑the‑minute quote, check one of the following reputable financial news sites:

| Source | Typical URL |
|--------|-------------|
| **Bloomberg** | https://www.bloomberg.com/markets/gold |
| **Reuters** | https://www.reuters.com/finance/commodities |
| **Kitco** | https://www.kitco.com/charts/livegold.html |
| **London Bullion Market Association (LBMA)** | https://lbma.org.uk |

These platforms update their gold pricing continuously throughout trading hours. If you’re looking at historical trends, most major exchanges report the U.S. dollar price per troy ounce, which has hovered between roughly $1,800–$2,300 over recent months depending on economic conditions.
message.reasoning:
The user asks "What is the gold price today in USA?" They want current gold price. We cannot browse internet; we can provide approximate typical range but not real-time data. According to policy, if it's about up-to-date info like stock prices, we should say can't fetch live data. So respond with explanation that I don't have access to real-time market data.

We might give general context: Gold spot price per ounce etc. But better to state inability to retrieve real-time data. Provide suggestion how to find it via reliable sources such as Bloomberg, Reuters, Kitco, NYMEX, etc. Also mention typical daily fluctuations around $2000/oz historically. Let's comply with policies.
